newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S.-Iraq conflict rocks Indian shares.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Iraq conflict rocks Indian shares.

text.p: Indian shares took a pounding on Tuesday as news of the U.S. missile attack on Iraq caught the market napping after prices opened higher, brokers said.
"That was the only reason for the crash," said Kamlesh Sanghavi, director at Sanghavi Savla Stock Brokers Ltd. "People were taken by surprise."
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange ended 78.30 points, or 2.20 percent, down at 3,484.68 after rising to 3,586.89 in early trade.
The Delhi share index index closed 17.91 points, or 2.2 percent, lower at 789.68.
Traders said the tumble was a "knee-jerk" reaction to the Middle-East crisis.
"The initial reaction was bad. We should see some discounting in a couple of days when the fears recede," said Ram Mohan at Lloyds Brokerage.
The setback came after the market started strongly in anticipation of a crucial speech by Chidambaram in parliament about 1996/97 (April-March) budget proposals.
Shortly before close Chidambaram put off his statement because of a disruption in parliament, and brokers said they were disappointed but hopeful.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index dropped 14 points to 1,037 with the net traded value at 12.44 billion rupees in 66.39 million shares.
The 500-share CRISIL index fell 10.30 points to 689.24.
On the BSE, TELCO fell 21 rupees to 501, ACC 49.25 to 2,163, Nestle 13.0 to 261, Hind Lever 15 to 812, BSES 7.50 to 197.50, Tata Power 6.0 to 150.75 and Grasim 9.50 to 434.50.
SBI and TISCO each dropped 6.50 rupees, to 276.25 and 193.50 respectively while Reliance eased 7.25 to 207.25.
The Calcutta index shed 5.07 points to 451.09 and the Madras index 15.72 points to 3,501.42.
